proof_summary: For \(2\le n\le4\), the congruence \(10^i\equiv1+9i\pmod{81}\), combined with reversal, shows that any number and its reverse both divisible by \(3^n\) must have digit sum divisible by \(3^n\); the digit-sum bound then forces the minimal candidate to be the corresponding all-nines number. For \(n\ge5\), a fixed 11-digit palindromic multiple of \(3^5\) is recursively concatenated threefold, each step adding a factor divisible by 3, producing a qualifying palindrome of length \(11\cdot3^{n-5}<3^{n-2}\) and hence strictly smaller than the all-nines number.
